item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00406","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C24","C05","C14"],"selected_candidate_label":"C24","confidence":0.91,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C24 plausibly supplied a material template. Both memoranda reject a private relief bill because the claimant failed to act within a statutory limitations period, explain why finality rules are administratively desirable, find no special equitable circumstances warranting an exception, and conclude that individualized relief would be discriminatory. C05 shares the broader private-bill argument against abrogating general law for one claimant, while C14 parallels the refusal to override a completed adjudicative process, but neither matches the child's limitations-based machinery as closely as C24.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Congress, in section 514 of the Tariff Act, has provided that if such a protest is not made within sixty days, the decision of the collector is final and conclusive","parent_excerpt":"The claim for refund filed in 1933 was rejected on the grounds it was not filed within the statutory period.","explanation":"Both identify the claimant's failure to use a prescribed remedy within the statutory period as the central legal obstacle."},{"child_excerpt":"This provision, like other statutes of limitations, is desirable to permit the final disposition of cases in an orderly manner.","parent_excerpt":"This unilateral statement ... illustrates the desirability of a statute of limitations which disposes of stale claims","explanation":"The child closely reproduces C24's policy justification for enforcing limitation periods, adapting it from stale tax claims to final customs classifications."},{"child_excerpt":"To grant relief in this situation would be inequitable and would discriminate against the hundreds of other importers","parent_excerpt":"the proposed legislation would be discriminatory and would single out a particular taxpayer for relief from the statute of limitations without adequate reason","explanation":"This is a distinctive shared conclusion: a private exception to a limitations rule would discriminatorily favor one claimant over similarly situated parties."}]}
